domain: Lunar New Year dinner for family
base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user plan their family's Lunar New Year dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any logistics. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're hosting Lunar New Year dinner at our place this year. It's going to be a big one — can you help me plan the menu?

flow_info.value: Coming so far: me and my husband, my parents (Mom and Dad), my sister Mei, and my brother-in-law Kevin
Dad's gout has been flaring up again, the doctor put him on medication and told him to watch what he eats
Kevin was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Mei just told us she's 4 months pregnant, everyone's so excited
Uncle Chen just confirmed he's coming too, flying in from Chengdu
Uncle Chen ate something with peanuts at a wedding two years ago and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Dad just came back from his checkup — doctor said his uric acid levels are back to normal, he's off the medication and cleared to eat whatever he wants
Mei just called — Kevin got food poisoning and is really sick, so they're not coming anymore. But Mei asked if I could save her a few containers of food, she'll pick them up the next day
Grandma decided she's coming after all! She's 87 and just got new dentures last month, still getting used to them — she told Mom she can only manage really soft foods right now
Menu to check: whole steamed fish, kung pao chicken, braised pork belly, salmon sashimi platter, longevity noodles, eight-treasure rice pudding

constraints.value: Must avoid high-purine foods: organ meats, shellfish, red meat in excess, alcohol, rich broths
constraints.surface_form: Dad's gout has been flaring up again, the doctor put him on medication and told him to watch what he eats
inference_chain: Elevated uric acid → must avoid high-purine foods
High-purine foods → organ meats, shellfish, excessive red meat, alcohol, rich broths

constraints.value: Cannot eat anything containing gluten: wheat, barley, rye, soy sauce (unless gluten-free), regular noodles, most dumpling wrappers
constraints.surface_form: Kevin was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
Many Chinese dishes use wheat noodles, soy sauce (contains wheat), dumpling wrappers

constraints.value: Should avoid raw fish/seafood, high-mercury fish, unpasteurized foods, excess caffeine, alcohol
constraints.surface_form: Mei just told us she's 4 months pregnant, everyone's so excited
inference_chain: 4 months pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions apply
Pregnancy → avoid raw fish/seafood (listeria/parasite risk), high-mercury fish, alcohol

constraints.surface_form: Uncle Chen ate something with peanuts at a wedding two years ago and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Throat swelled up after eating peanuts → allergic reaction
Severe peanut allergy → must avoid all peanut and peanut-derived ingredients

constraints.value: Can only eat soft foods due to new dentures
constraints.surface_form: Grandma just got new dentures last month, still getting used to them — she told Mom she can only manage really soft foods right now

hidden_state.value: You are hosting Lunar New Year dinner at your home. You will introduce family members and their situations across several turns. Plans will change — some people drop out, some join late, one person's health restriction gets lifted. At the end you will present a specific menu and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER hint at which dishes are problematic or tell the assistant what to check for.

You are a warm, easygoing family organizer. You always refer to family members by name or relation in third person (e.g. 'Dad told me...', 'Mei just called...'). You never express frustration or impatience when plans change — it's just how family gatherings go. You treat each update as normal family coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for family updates

aims.success_criteria: Agent checks each dish against current constraint state: kung pao chicken contains peanuts (Uncle Chen anaphylaxis), salmon sashimi is raw fish (cannot save for Mei who is pregnant), longevity noodles contain wheat (Kevin had celiac but Kevin is no longer coming so this is fine), whole steamed fish may be hard for Grandma's dentures, braised pork belly is fine (Dad's gout is cleared), eight-treasure rice pudding is soft and generally safe

ground_truth.answer: Kung pao chicken is problematic: it contains peanuts, and Uncle Chen has a severe peanut allergy (anaphylaxis, required EpiPen). Salmon sashimi platter is problematic for the table if Grandma eats it raw (texture may be OK but raw fish is unusual for elderly), and critically it must NOT be saved for Mei because she is 4 months pregnant and should avoid raw fish. Whole steamed fish may be difficult for Grandma who can only eat soft foods right now due to new dentures — steamed fish can be soft but may have bones that are hard to manage with new dentures, worth flagging. Braised pork belly is fine — Dad's gout restriction has been lifted, he is cleared to eat anything. Longevity noodles are fine — Kevin had celiac disease but Kevin is no longer coming, so gluten is not a concern for anyone at the table. Eight-treasure rice pudding is fine — soft, no peanuts, no raw ingredients, suitable for everyone including Grandma.
required_elements: Kung pao chicken is problematic because it contains peanuts and Uncle Chen has a severe peanut allergy (throat swelled up, needed EpiPen)
Salmon sashimi platter must not be saved/packed for Mei because she is 4 months pregnant and should avoid raw fish
Whole steamed fish may pose difficulty for Grandma due to her new dentures and need for soft foods
Braised pork belly is fine — Dad's gout restriction has been lifted after his checkup showed normal uric acid levels
Longevity noodles are fine for everyone at the table — Kevin had celiac but he is no longer attending
Eight-treasure rice pudding is fine for everyone currently attending
forbidden_elements: Flagging longevity noodles as problematic for gluten (Kevin is no longer coming, his celiac constraint is removed from the table)
Flagging braised pork belly as problematic for Dad's gout (his restriction has been lifted by his doctor)
Completely rejecting salmon sashimi (it is only problematic for Mei's saved food due to pregnancy, fine for the table)
Saying Uncle Chen has a general nut allergy or tree nut allergy (he specifically has a peanut allergy)
Flagging any dish for Kevin's celiac disease (Kevin is not attending and does not need food saved)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking with scope changes across a Lunar New Year family dinner. The agent must track: (1) Uncle Chen joins late with a severe peanut allergy inferred from the EpiPen anecdote — kung pao chicken contains peanuts and is dangerous for him. (2) Dad's gout restriction is REMOVED mid-conversation after his doctor clears him — braised pork belly is now fine. (3) Mei and Kevin EXIT the dinner, but Mei wants food saved for the next day — her pregnancy constraint (no raw fish) still applies to saved food, while Kevin's celiac constraint is fully removed since he gets no food. (4) Grandma joins late with a soft food constraint from new dentures — whole steamed fish with bones may be problematic. (5) Longevity noodles are a trap: they contain wheat gluten which would be bad for Kevin's celiac, but Kevin is no longer coming and no food is being saved for him, so noodles are fine. (6) Salmon sashimi requires scope distinction: fine for the table, but must not be packed for Mei due to pregnancy. The over-generalization trap is treating Uncle Chen's peanut allergy as a general nut allergy, or treating Mei's exit as removing her constraint entirely when she still needs food saved.

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
